about.summary: EDvance College is a nonprofit institution of higher education located in San Francisco, California, focused on early childhood education. The college offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Early Childhood Studies and various certificates for educators. It is accredited by the WASC Senior College and University Commission.

documents.title: Institutional Data
documents.summary: EDvance College is focused on building a skilled workforce of early childhood educators by offering affordable and accessible education programs. The institution shares data on student demographics, enrollment, employment, and language for the academic years 2023-2025, emphasizing commitment through annual impact reports. EDvance is accredited by WSCUC.

documents.title: Institutional Data
documents.summary: EDvance College provides accessible, high-quality programs for early childhood educators, addressing the shortage of skilled professionals in the field. In the 2024 academic year, they served a diverse body of students, many of whom are employed in early childhood roles across multiple counties. The college has a high graduation rate and significant participation of first-generation students. The latest Impact Reports highlight the progress made in education access and workforce development, with a strong commitment to overcoming barriers and advancing the careers of educators.

documents.title: Institutional Data
documents.summary: EDvance College aims to address the shortage of skilled early childhood educators through high-quality, accessible programs. This page contains data on the student body, retention and graduation rates, demographics, and employment details. The 2024-2025 academic year highlights progress in increasing enrollment, diversity, and supporting workforce development. EDvance College published its Impact Reports showcasing progress and commitment to empowerment through education.

documents.title: EDvance College Glossary
documents.summary: The EDvance College Glossary provides definitions of key terms related to the institution's innovative educational model for early childhood educators. These terms describe student groupings (cohort model), structured progress toward graduation (degree pathway), and unique learning methodologies like shorter semesters, live group learning, and employer placements.
